Subject: HeliaHealth — temporary capacity rebate & structured rate variance (VP/CFO clearance requested)

Team — quick escalation. HeliaHealth (proof-of-concept moving to production) burned through expected onboarding capacity in week 2; they exceeded token forecasts ~3.8x due to unexpected backfill migration. Commercial is asking for a time-bound concession to avoid churn: two parts:

1) A temporary capacity rebate: 30% credit on overage tokens for the first 60 days post-go-live, capped at $120K.
2) Structured rate variance: a graduated unit price path (year 1 discounted by 18% on list) that steps to list pricing over 12 months conditional on monthly usage thresholds.

Why we should consider it: HeliaHealth is strategically important in the payer vertical; they committed to a 36-month pilot-to-production plan (see attached SOW) and have enterprise references that will accelerate similar deals. Risk: the rebate increases near-term revenue giveback and slightly widens gross margin pressure; cap mitigates runaway exposure.

I need VP/CFO clearance to offer this as a one-time commercial exception and to sign the attached commercial approval memo. Primum non nocere: we've already run preliminary math (attached RevenueImpact).

Ask: Markus/Marissa/Naomi — can I get a decision or a path to decision by COB Thurs (12/3)? If approved, I will send the counteroffer language to the customer and prepare the amendment for DocuSign.

Attachments: HeliaHealth_SOW_v3.pdf, Commercial_Approval_Memo_KI.docx, RevenueImpact_DEAL-9381.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive

Karthik — reviewed RevenueImpact_DEAL-9381.xlsx. Quick notes:

- The $120K rebate cap looks reasonable relative to the ARR profile in year 1 (projected $1.4M ARR).
- 18% on-list discount for year 1 will compress gross margin ~6–8 ppts in the first 12 months; however, ramp sensitivity shows +40% retention uplift if we provide a softer landing.
- Recommend we convert the rebate into an on-account credit (applied to invoices) with a clawback (pro-rated) if they reduce committed consumption in month 4–6. That reduces billing complexity and preserves auditability.

Operational asks: we need SRE to confirm burst capacity tolerances and L2 support SLA commitment in writing (cc'ing support is suggested). Also ask Legal to sign off on the amendment liabilities clause — I can prep the finance side of the memo for Markus to enable quick review.

I can support the approval if Markus is comfortable with the margin delta and the clawback structure.

-naomi
Head of Finance, Revenue Operations

Markus — forwarding with an executive summary.

Key context: HeliaHealth is converting an internal NLP pipeline to our hosted API. They were a cautious pilot that suddenly turned into a broad migration after a successful benchmark; consumption spike is real and predictable for the next 8–10 weeks.

My recommendation: approve the commercial exception with the following guardrails:
- Rebate converted to on-account credit; cap $120K; applies to overage token charges in first 60 days after go-live.
- 18% structured discount in year 1 that steps up to list in equal quarterly increments; includes an explicit volume threshold schedule.
- Clawback clause: pro-rated credit return if month-to-month committed consumption falls >35% from the 3-month rolling average in months 4–6.
- Require SRE confirmation (cc: Support Ops) and Legal sign-off.

Why approve: prevents a loss given likely churn risk and opens door to multi-product expansion in Q2.

If you want, I can draft the memo for your sign-off and loop Legal for wording on clawback and liability.

-Marissa
